If `compile_context` rejects a packet, **that invocation fails**; other calls are affected only if their own packets are rejected.

- **Direct path:** `compile_evidence_bundle` calls `compile_context` and propagates its `ContextError` with `?`. Its direct production callers are `compile_certified_bundle` and the non-retry branch of MCP’s `compile_weavatrix`. The certified path also calls the separate layered compiler, which reaches `compile_context` through the same internal function. [context.rs](trace-sol-off/crates/cortex-weavatrix/src/compile/context.rs:34) [context.rs](trace-sol-off/crates/cortex-weavatrix/src/compile/context.rs:152) [certified.rs](trace-sol-off/crates/cortex-weavatrix/src/compile/certified.rs:35) [compile_session.rs](trace-sol-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/runtime/compile_session.rs:47)
- **User-facing effects through that path:** `weavatrix_context_compile`, `cortex_prepare`, and `cortex_expand` fail when their compile is rejected. The latter two are the default **Agent** profile’s tools; the Weavatrix tool is exposed by the **Context** and **Full** profiles. [context_tools.rs](trace-sol-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/context_tools.rs:88) [agent_tools.rs](trace-sol-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/agent_tools.rs:138) [agent_tools.rs](trace-sol-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/agent_tools.rs:317) [lib.rs](trace-sol-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/lib.rs:328)
- **Separate direct effect:** `context_compile` calls `compile_context` directly, so it can fail too, but **not through** `compile_evidence_bundle`. Compile errors become strings and then `ToolReply::error`; no evidence packet is returned on that path. [context_tools.rs](trace-sol-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/context_tools.rs:56) [compile_session.rs](trace-sol-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/runtime/compile_session.rs:58) [agent_tools.rs](trace-sol-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/agent_tools.rs:87)
- **HTTP:** The HTTP transport uses the same tool registry and forwards the MCP reply as JSON with **HTTP 200**. A compiler rejection is therefore surfaced as a tool error in the response body, not as an HTTP error status. [http.rs](trace-sol-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/runtime/http.rs:47) [http.rs](trace-sol-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/runtime/http.rs:180)

**Packet:** `pk_5f8b3f2b996e` supplied the `compile_evidence_bundle` definition. Its coverage certificate reported no missing facets, so it offered nothing to expand. It did not cover the caller chain or HTTP error path; I checked those in source. I found no wrong packet evidence.

`compile_evidence_bundle` calls `compile_layered`, which calls `compile_context` and propagates its error with `?`. Its **direct production callers** are `compile_certified_bundle` and the plain branch of `compile_weavatrix`; the certified path can also fail during a later layered compile. [context.rs](trace-sol-on/crates/cortex-weavatrix/src/compile/context.rs:34), [context.rs](trace-sol-on/crates/cortex-weavatrix/src/compile/context.rs:152), [certified.rs](trace-sol-on/crates/cortex-weavatrix/src/compile/certified.rs:35), [compile_session.rs](trace-sol-on/crates/cortex-mcp/src/runtime/compile_session.rs:47).

If the affected packets are newly rejected, **`weavatrix_context_compile` fails through `compile_weavatrix`; `cortex_prepare` and `cortex_expand` fail transitively through that same function.** The separate `context_compile` tool calls `compile_context` directly, so it is affected independently. Each handler turns the error string into `ToolReply::error`; a failed prepare or expansion does not return its packet. [context_tools.rs](trace-sol-on/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/context_tools.rs:56), [context_tools.rs](trace-sol-on/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/context_tools.rs:88), [agent_tools.rs](trace-sol-on/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/agent_tools.rs:87), [agent_tools.rs](trace-sol-on/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/agent_tools.rs:112), [agent_tools.rs](trace-sol-on/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/agent_tools.rs:317).

The default **agent profile** exposes only `cortex_prepare` and `cortex_expand`; the context profile exposes the two context tools, and full exposes both sets. HTTP `/mcp` uses the selected profile and passes the tool’s JSON-RPC reply through as an HTTP 200 response. A compiler rejection therefore surfaces as a tool error in that reply, not as an HTTP transport status error. [lib.rs](trace-sol-on/crates/cortex-mcp/src/lib.rs:292), [lib.rs](trace-sol-on/crates/cortex-mcp/src/lib.rs:328), [http.rs](trace-sol-on/crates/cortex-mcp/src/runtime/http.rs:48), [http.rs](trace-sol-on/crates/cortex-mcp/src/runtime/http.rs:180).

The **direct caller** of `compile_context` on the Weavatrix path is `compile_evidence_bundle`, which propagates its `ContextError` with `?` ([context.rs](trace-luna-off/crates/cortex-weavatrix/src/compile/context.rs:34), [context.rs](trace-luna-off/crates/cortex-weavatrix/src/compile/context.rs:152)). In the MCP runtime, `compile_weavatrix` calls that function on its ordinary path, and calls `compile_certified_bundle` when gathering returns a retry report; it converts either compile error to a string ([compile_session.rs](trace-luna-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/runtime/compile_session.rs:47), [compile_session.rs](trace-luna-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/runtime/compile_session.rs:60)). The certified path also calls `compile_evidence_bundle` directly, then layered variants that ultimately call `compile_context` ([certified.rs](trace-luna-off/crates/cortex-weavatrix/src/compile/certified.rs:35), [context.rs](trace-luna-off/crates/cortex-weavatrix/src/compile/context.rs:46)).

On the **agent profile**, `cortex_prepare` and `cortex_expand` both reach `compile_weavatrix` with `targeted: true`; so a new rejection can fail either user-facing call. `cortex_prepare` does so via `prepare_packet` ([agent_tools.rs](trace-luna-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/agent_tools.rs:124), [agent_tools.rs](trace-luna-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/agent_tools.rs:138)); `cortex_expand` does so via `expand_packet` ([agent_tools.rs](trace-luna-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/agent_tools.rs:302), [agent_tools.rs](trace-luna-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/agent_tools.rs:317)). The profile exposes those two tools ([lib.rs](trace-luna-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/lib.rs:293), [lib.rs](trace-luna-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/lib.rs:334)). The error reaches each handler as a string and is returned as `ToolReply::error` ([agent_tools.rs](trace-luna-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/agent_tools.rs:91), [agent_tools.rs](trace-luna-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/agent_tools.rs:112)).

**HTTP is transitive transport**, not another compiler caller: it builds the selected profile’s same server ([http.rs](trace-luna-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/runtime/http.rs:47), [http.rs](trace-luna-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/runtime/http.rs:56)) and returns its JSON-RPC reply in an HTTP 200 JSON response ([http.rs](trace-luna-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/runtime/http.rs:180)). Thus the compile failure is surfaced as a tool error in the MCP reply, not as an HTTP error status.

Separately, the full/context profiles expose `weavatrix_context_compile`, which is another **transitive** `compile_weavatrix` path; and `context_compile` directly calls `compile_context` on caller-supplied items ([context_tools.rs](trace-luna-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/context_tools.rs:14), [context_tools.rs](trace-luna-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/context_tools.rs:61), [context_tools.rs](trace-luna-off/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/context_tools.rs:68)). A rejection affects those calls when they encounter the rejected packets; `context_compile` is not on the agent profile path.

`compile_evidence_bundle` builds evidence items and passes them to `compile_context`; a rejection propagates as `ContextError` at [compile/context.rs:148-156](trace-luna-on/crates/cortex-weavatrix/src/compile/context.rs:148). `compile_context` returns validation or budget errors, including `TooManyItems` and `CriticalItemExceedsBudget` ([context/lib.rs:103-125](trace-luna-on/crates/cortex-context/src/lib.rs:103), [context/lib.rs:181-239](trace-luna-on/crates/cortex-context/src/lib.rs:181)).

**User-facing effects**

- **Direct callers of `compile_context`:** `compile_evidence_bundle` and the `context_compile` tool ([context_tools.rs:56-64](trace-luna-on/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/context_tools.rs:56)). The tool is exposed in the Context and Full profiles; it is not exposed in Agent ([lib.rs:328-346](trace-luna-on/crates/cortex-mcp/src/lib.rs:328)).
- **Transitive effects through `compile_evidence_bundle`:** Agent-profile `cortex_prepare` calls `compile_weavatrix` ([agent_tools.rs:124-150](trace-luna-on/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/agent_tools.rs:124)); `cortex_expand` also calls it when compiling the requested facet ([agent_tools.rs:302-329](trace-luna-on/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/agent_tools.rs:302)). The legacy `weavatrix_context_compile` tool shares this path ([context_tools.rs:88-107](trace-luna-on/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/context_tools.rs:88)).
- **Error surface:** These handlers convert failures to `ToolReply::error`; MCP clients receive a tool-level error ([agent_tools.rs:87-94](trace-luna-on/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/agent_tools.rs:87), [context_tools.rs:56-64](trace-luna-on/crates/cortex-mcp/src/tools/context_tools.rs:56)). Over HTTP, the transport relays the JSON-RPC reply in an HTTP 200 response; transport/session failures have separate HTTP statuses ([http.rs:180-198](trace-luna-on/crates/cortex-mcp/src/runtime/http.rs:180)).

**Packet:** `pk_6fc4a8bfa3f9`. Its certificate was sufficient and not stale. It helped identify the `compile_evidence_bundle` definition and the `compile_context` search match, but it did not establish the callers, profile exposure, or HTTP error path. The packet omitted two evidence items (441 estimated tokens); it offered no missing facets to expand. No wrong evidence was apparent.
